title: Protecting your photos in a digital age
titleChinese: 如何在数字时代保管你的照片
paragraphs: "Say cheese!" That's what the person behind the camera might shout when they want you to smile for a photo. 2025 marked the 50th anniversary of digital photography. Steve Sasson, inventor of the first digital camera in 1975, told the BBC that it looked like a 'toaster with a lens' - not like the stylish cameras we see today! By 2005, more people were buying digital cameras than film cameras, which meant that a process which used to be slow and laborious, was now quick and easy.

The 2000s brought a snap-happy era, with people now able to take hundreds, even thousands of photos a year. But what they hadn't quite worked out yet was how to store them. Back then, people used a mishmash of hard drives, USB sticks and CDs - physical storage that was at risk of loss or theft. Later came online photo sharing via social media or free online photo galleries where you can upload photos to 'the cloud'. The problem is that if you chose just one of these options for photo storage, such as an old laptop that's now broken, or a social media website that no longer exists, you may have what's called a 'black hole' in your photographic record, with no photos of life in the noughties. So, what's the advice?

After losing an external hard drive with all her family photos, Cathi Nelson set up The Photo Managers, a company which helps people manage their photo collections. They say the best protection is their '3-2-1' rule of photo storage which involves having three copies of each photo, all in different places. One in the cloud, the second on a hard drive, and a third on a drive in a separate location, like someone else's house. If that sounds like too much work, just make sure your smartphone automatically uploads photos to the cloud, and then spare some time once a month to upload those to a hard drive. And if you're someone who takes hundreds of photos per month, it's also a good idea to regularly curate your camera roll - keep the best ones and delete the rest, so you feel more in control.

The key takeaway here is that each storage method has its pitfalls, so it's better to always use two methods over just one in order to have a backup. Online platforms can be shut down, and hard drives can be lost. Just make sure your memories don't fade into the digital black hole.
chineseParagraphs: 说茄子！”当相机后面的人想让你为拍照而微笑时，可能会喊这句话。2025年标志着数码摄影诞生50周年。1975年第一台数码相机的发明者史蒂夫·萨松告诉BBC，它看起来像一个“带镜头的烤面包机”，而不是我们今天看到的时尚相机！到2005年，购买数码相机的人数超过了购买胶片相机的人数，这意味着过去缓慢而费力的过程变得快捷方便。

21世纪初带来了一个热衷于拍照的时代，人们现在每年能拍摄数百甚至数千张照片。但他们当时还没完全搞明白的是如何存储这些照片。那时，人们使用硬盘、U盘和CD等各种物理存储设备，这些设备存在丢失或被盗的风险。后来，你可以将照片上传到“云端”进行在线照片分享，通过社交媒体或免费在线相册。问题是，如果你只选择了其中一种照片存储方式，比如一台现在坏掉的旧笔记本电脑，或者一个已经不复存在的社交媒体网站，你的照片记录中可能会出现所谓的“黑洞”，丢失了那个十年里的生活照片。那么，有什么建议呢？

在丢失了一个存有所有家庭照片的外置硬盘后，凯西·尼尔森创立了The Photo Managers，一家帮助人们管理照片收藏的公司。他们表示，最好的保护方法是他们的“3-2-1”照片存储规则，即每张照片保存三份副本，存放在不同的地方。一份在云端，第二份在硬盘上，第三份在另一个地点的驱动器上，比如别人家里。如果这听起来太麻烦，只需确保你的智能手机自动将照片上传到云端，然后每月抽时间将那些照片上传到硬盘一次。如果你是一个每月拍摄数百张照片的人，定期整理你的手机相册也是个好主意——保留最好的，删除其余的，这样你会更有一切尽在掌握的感觉。
这里的关键是，每种存储方式都有其隐患，所以最好总是使用两种方法而不是一种，以便有备份。在线平台可能关闭，硬盘可能丢失。务必确保你的记忆不会消失在数字黑洞中。

vocabulary.entry: anniversary /ˌænɪˈvɜːsəri/ n. 周年纪念日
vocabulary.example: They celebrated their 20th wedding anniversary.
vocabulary.translation: 他们庆祝了结婚二十周年纪念日。

vocabulary.entry: digital photography /ˌdɪdʒɪtl fəˈtɒɡrəfi/ n. 数码摄影（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Digital photography has made it easy to share images instantly.
vocabulary.translation: 数码摄影让即时分享影像变得容易。

vocabulary.entry: toaster /ˈtəʊstə(r)/ n. 烤面包机
vocabulary.example: She popped two slices of bread into the toaster.
vocabulary.translation: 她把两片面包放进烤面包机里。

vocabulary.entry: lens /lenz/ n. 镜头
vocabulary.example: The camera has a wide-angle lens.
vocabulary.translation: 这台相机有一个广角镜头。

vocabulary.entry: stylish /ˈstaɪlɪʃ/ adj. 时尚的，有风格的
vocabulary.example: She wore a stylish black dress.
vocabulary.translation: 她穿了一条时尚的黑色连衣裙。

vocabulary.entry: laborious /ləˈbɔːriəs/ adj. 费力的，辛苦的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The work was laborious and time-consuming.
vocabulary.translation: 这项工作费时费力。

vocabulary.entry: snap-happy /ˈsnæp hæpi/ adj. 热衷于拍照的（口语）
vocabulary.example: A snap-happy tourist takes photos of everything.
vocabulary.translation: 一个热衷于拍照的游客会拍下一切。

vocabulary.entry: work out /ˌwɜːk ˈaʊt/ phr. v. 想出，弄明白（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: We need to work out a better way to save water.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要想出一个更好的节水方法。

vocabulary.definition: 混杂物，杂乱的一堆（口语）
vocabulary.entry: mishmash /ˈmɪʃmæʃ/ n. 混杂物，杂乱的一堆（口语）
vocabulary.example: The report is a mishmash of facts and opinions.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告是事实和观点的杂乱混合。

vocabulary.entry: hard drive /ˈhɑːd draɪv/ n. 硬盘（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He saved the files to an external hard drive.
vocabulary.translation: 他把文件存到了外置硬盘上。

vocabulary.entry: USB stick /ˌjuː es ˈbiː stɪk/ n. U盘，闪存盘（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She copied the presentation onto a USB stick.
vocabulary.translation: 她把演示文稿复制到了U盘上。

vocabulary.entry: theft /θeft/ n. 盗窃，偷盗（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The car was damaged in an attempted theft.
vocabulary.translation: 这辆车在一次未遂盗窃中被损坏。

vocabulary.definition: 画廊，展览馆；相册（此处指在线相册）
vocabulary.entry: gallery /ˈɡæləri/ n. 画廊，展览馆；相册（此处指在线相册）
vocabulary.example: The museum has a new gallery of modern art.
vocabulary.translation: 博物馆有一个新的现代艺术展厅。

vocabulary.entry: upload /ˌʌpˈləʊd/ v. 上传
vocabulary.example: You can upload your photos to the cloud.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以将照片上传到云端。

vocabulary.entry: cloud /klaʊd/ n. 云端（计算术语）
vocabulary.example: I store all my documents in the cloud.
vocabulary.translation: 我把所有文件都存储在云端。

vocabulary.entry: option /ˈɒpʃn/ n. 选择，选项
vocabulary.example: There are several options on the menu.
vocabulary.translation: 菜单上有几种选择。

vocabulary.entry: laptop /ˈlæptɒp/ n. 笔记本电脑
vocabulary.example: She works on her laptop in cafes.
vocabulary.translation: 她在咖啡馆里用手提电脑工作。

vocabulary.definition: 黑洞（此处比喻信息的丢失）（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: black hole /ˌblæk ˈhəʊl/ n. 黑洞（此处比喻信息的丢失）（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The missing files vanished into a digital black hole.
vocabulary.translation: 丢失的文件消失在了数字黑洞中。

vocabulary.entry: noughties /ˈnɔːtiz/ n. 21世纪头十年（2000-2009年）（口语）
vocabulary.example: She was a teenager in the noughties.
vocabulary.translation: 她在二十一世纪头十年还是青少年。

vocabulary.entry: external /ɪkˈstɜːnl/ adj. 外部的，外接的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The computer has an external hard drive.
vocabulary.translation: 这台电脑有一个外接硬盘。

vocabulary.entry: set up /ˌset ˈʌp/ phr. v. 建立，创立（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She set up her own company after graduation.
vocabulary.translation: 她毕业后创办了自己的公司。

vocabulary.entry: collection /kəˈlekʃn/ n. 收藏，收集
vocabulary.example: He has a large collection of stamps.
vocabulary.translation: 他有大量的邮票收藏。

vocabulary.entry: protection /prəˈtekʃn/ n. 保护，防护
vocabulary.example: The sunscreen provides protection against UV rays.
vocabulary.translation: 这款防晒霜提供防紫外线保护。

vocabulary.entry: copy /ˈkɒpi/ n. 副本，拷贝
vocabulary.example: Always keep a backup copy of important documents.
vocabulary.translation: 始终保留重要文件的备份副本。

vocabulary.entry: automatically /ˌɔːtəˈmætɪkli/ adv. 自动地
vocabulary.example: The camera focuses automatically.
vocabulary.translation: 相机自动对焦。

vocabulary.entry: spare /speə(r)/ v. 腾出（时间），抽出（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Can you spare a few minutes to talk?
vocabulary.translation: 你能抽出几分钟谈谈吗？

vocabulary.entry: curate /kjʊəˈreɪt/ v. 策划，整理（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She curated a collection of modern art for the museum.
vocabulary.translation: 她为博物馆策划了一个现代艺术收藏。

vocabulary.definition: 相机胶卷，手机相册（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: camera roll /ˈkæmərə rəʊl/ n. 相机胶卷，手机相册（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I deleted a few blurry photos from my camera roll.
vocabulary.translation: 我从手机相册中删除了几张模糊的照片。

vocabulary.entry: in control /ɪn kənˈtrəʊl/ phr. 在掌控之中（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She felt more in control after making a plan.
vocabulary.translation: 制定计划后她感觉更有掌控感。

vocabulary.definition: 要点，关键信息（此处为引申义）
vocabulary.entry: takeaway /ˈteɪkəweɪ/ n. 要点，关键信息（此处为引申义）
vocabulary.example: The key takeaway from the meeting is that we need more staff.
vocabulary.translation: 这次会议的关键信息是我们需要更多的人手。

vocabulary.entry: pitfall /ˈpɪtfɔːl/ n. 隐患，陷阱（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The project has many potential pitfalls.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目有很多潜在的陷阱。

vocabulary.entry: backup /ˈbækʌp/ n. 备份（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Always have a backup of your important files.
vocabulary.translation: 始终备份你的重要文件。

vocabulary.entry: platform /ˈplætfɔːm/ n. 平台（尤指社交媒体）
vocabulary.example: The company launched its new social media platform.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司推出了新的社交媒体平台。

vocabulary.definition: 关闭，停止运营（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: shut down /ˌʃʌt ˈdaʊn/ phr. v. 关闭，停止运营（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The factory was shut down due to a lack of funding.
vocabulary.translation: 由于缺乏资金，这家工厂被关闭了。

vocabulary.definition: 逐渐消失在……中（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: fade into /ˈfeɪd ɪntə/ phr. v. 逐渐消失在……中（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The ship faded into the fog.
vocabulary.translation: 船逐渐消失在雾中。
